_about: Describes every Amass configuration setting so the AI config assistant can explain settings and propose changes grounded in the schema, not in hardcoded prose. Paths use dots: scope.domains, options.database. The transformations.* and datasources.* entries describe the per-item fields of a FROM->TO transformation and of a data source. A test fails when a config struct field or documented option has no entry here, so add an entry when a field is added. Nothing here enables collection or names a specific target; it only describes the schema.

sections.seed: Where an enumeration starts: the existing knowledge about the target (its domains, known names, address space, or company). The one section you really need; every seed entry is also in scope.
sections.scope: The boundary a discovered asset must fall within to be kept. The engine may widen it as evidence appears, as far as the expansion policy (each transformation's reach and confidence) allows, so it is a starting boundary, not a hard cap.
sections.options: Operational settings: the database, the engine, DNS resolvers, brute-force and alteration wordlists, active-probe pacing, and how long a run keeps working on background collection.
sections.transformations: Which Open Asset Model asset-type transitions the engine collects, and each one's TTL, confidence, priority, excluded data sources and expansion policy (reach). A key is FROM->TO, where TO is an asset type, ALL (every transition from that type), NONE (collect nothing from that type), or a data source name. The one other key, default, holds the values a transition takes when neither it nor its FROM->ALL sets them.
sections.datasources: The external data sources and their per-source credentials and TTLs, kept in the datasources.yaml file named by options.datasources.
sections.ai: Optional model, classifier and attribution settings, set under options.ai. Advisory only; it never turns AI on by itself, and enumeration needs no model.

active.description: Whether active collection is allowed: zone transfers, certificate name grabs and service probes that contact the target directly. Passive collection is the default. The -active command-line flag sets it.

background_hold.description: How long an enumeration keeps working on background collection once its other work is done. The web archives (Wayback Machine, Common Crawl) can take an hour to answer for a big domain, so they are read beside the pipeline, one domain at a time, and never stall it. A domain still waiting when the hold runs out is left for the next run, and the log says so. 0 waits for none: the archives are read only while the run has other work.

scope.domains.description: Registered domains allowed in scope. A name is in scope when it is one of these or a subdomain of one.

scope.ips.type: list of IP addresses and ranges
scope.ips.description: IP addresses allowed in scope. Single addresses, dash ranges (192.0.2.3-8) and full ranges (192.0.2.10-192.0.2.20) are accepted.

scope.cidrs.description: CIDR ranges allowed in scope; an address inside one is in scope.

scope.asns.description: Autonomous system numbers allowed in scope; the networks they announce are in scope.

scope.organizations.description: Organizations (corporations) discovered assets must be attributable to. In the seed, a starting point the engine resolves to the company's domains, networks and systems.

scope.phones.description: Seed only. Phone numbers the enumeration starts from; the engine resolves each to the organizations tied to the number and their domains. A number pivots to organizations, it does not bound the scope.

scope.street_addresses.description: Seed only. Street addresses the enumeration starts from; the engine resolves each to the organizations at the address and their domains. A shared or registered-agent address is held for review rather than enumerated.

scope.ports.description: Ports active enumeration may probe on in-scope addresses. Omit to probe every port the probes know; list ports only to narrow that. Ranges such as 8000-8010 work.

scope.blacklist.description: Subdomains that will never be investigated, even when otherwise in scope.

scope.names.description: Seed only. Known DNS names (leads), usually subdomains of an in-scope domain, supplied so the enumeration does not overlook them. Each lead's registered domain is added to the scope. The -nf flag adds names the same way.

scope.names_file.description: Seed only. A file of seed DNS names, one per line; its names are treated as leads like seed.names.

options.datasources.description: Path to the datasources.yaml file holding data source credentials and TTLs.

options.database.default: a local SQLite database under the output directory
options.database.description: The asset database connection string. PostgreSQL (postgres://...) and Neo4j (neo4j://... or bolt://...) are supported; without this a local SQLite database is used.

options.engine.default: http://127.0.0.1:4000 (a local engine is started when none is given)
options.engine.description: URL of the collection engine the client connects to.

options.resolvers.type: list of IP addresses or files
options.resolvers.description: DNS resolvers the enumeration's queries go to: IP addresses with an optional port, or files listing one per line. Without them the trusted resolvers take the queries, and without either the engine's default public resolvers do. The -r and -rf flags set it.

options.trusted_resolvers.type: list of IP addresses or files
options.trusted_resolvers.description: Trusted DNS resolvers: the first tests for DNS wildcards, and they take the queries when resolvers is not set. The -tr flag sets it.

options.interface.description: The network interface on the engine's host that the enumeration's traffic (HTTP, DNS, WHOIS and probes) leaves through: an interface name or one of the host's IP addresses. Without it, the engine's -iface setting (AMASS_IFACE) applies. The -iface flag sets it.

options.active_route.description: The route active traffic (certificate, banner and HTTP probes, JARM and zone transfers) takes: an interface on the engine's host, or a proxy URL: socks5h://host:port (the proxy resolves names, as Tor needs), socks5://host:port or http://host:port (CONNECT). A proxy carries TCP only; active traffic never falls back to a direct connection, and a refusal by the proxy or a Tor exit is not taken as evidence about the target. Without it, the engine's -active-route setting (AMASS_ACTIVE_ROUTE) applies. The -active-route flag sets it.

options.active_udp_route.description: The interface active UDP traffic leaves from when the active route is a proxy, which cannot carry UDP. Without it, active UDP is not sent through a proxy route. The -active-udp-route flag sets it.

options.bruteforce.description: DNS brute forcing: enabled on/off and the wordlist files it uses.

options.alterations.description: Name alteration generation: enabled on/off and the wordlist files it uses.

options.minimum_ttl.description: The smallest TTL applied to data source responses; a source's shorter TTL is raised to this.

options.background_hold.description: How long a run keeps working on background collection, such as the web archives' slow queries, once its other work is done. 0 waits for none: the archives are read only while the run has other work. What is still queued when it ends is left for the next run, and the log says so.

options.probe_pace_ms.description: Minimum spacing between active probes to one host, so a host is not reached by a burst across ports. 0 turns pacing off. Only hosts you control should be probed without pacing.

options.probe_jitter_ms.description: Additional random spread added to the probe pace, so a host's probes do not arrive on a fixed rhythm.

options.probe_timeout_ms.description: How long an active probe waits to connect to a host's port before giving up. Ports are probed one at a time per host, so a filtered or dead port waits out this whole duration; this is the main lever on how long active enumeration takes against unresponsive hosts. 0 or less uses the default.

transformations.default.description: Defaults applied to a transformation that does not set its own ttl, confidence, priority or reach (after its FROM->ALL). A reach here is the whole configuration's expansion policy, which transformations can then narrow or widen. It is the one transformations entry without FROM->TO.

transformations.ttl.description: How long a FROM->TO result is reused before it is collected again. A larger value re-collects less often.

transformations.confidence.description: The minimum confidence the evidence needs before an asset reached through this transition is admitted into scope. A higher value widens the scope only on stronger evidence; above 100, nothing is admitted through it.

transformations.priority.description: The relative order in which this transition runs; lower runs sooner.

transformations.exclude.description: Data sources not to use for this transition, when the rest are still wanted.

transformations.reach.description: The expansion policy for this transition: where an asset must stand for it to run. scope: within the scope the run was given; footprint: in scope, including what the run admitted; connected: linked to the footprint within hops; any: every asset. A transition without one takes its FROM->ALL reach, then transformations.default.

transformations.hops.description: With reach: connected, how many relations away from the footprint an asset may be.

datasources.name.description: The data source the entry configures, matching a source Amass knows.

datasources.ttl.description: How long this source's responses are reused before the source is queried again.

datasources.creds.type: object of named credential sets {username, password, apikey, secret}
datasources.creds.description: The source's credentials. Secrets are entered by the operator, never by a model.

options.ai.provider.description: The main model's provider for amass ai questions and review: ollama (native API), compatible (an OpenAI-compatible chat API) or anthropic. AMASS_LLM_PROVIDER overrides it.

options.ai.endpoint.description: The main model's endpoint. The Compose Ollama is http://ollama:11434 (ollama) or http://ollama:11434/v1/chat/completions (compatible). AMASS_LLM_ENDPOINT overrides it.

options.ai.model.description: The main model's name at the provider. Without it, amass ai answers only the questions that need no model. AMASS_LLM_MODEL overrides it.

options.ai.api_key_env.description: The environment variable holding a hosted provider's API key. The key itself never goes in the config.

options.ai.allow_http.description: Allows a plain HTTP model endpoint other than localhost, for a trusted private network only (such as the Compose network).

options.ai.model_timeout.description: How long one main model request may take.

options.ai.investigation_timeout.description: How long one question may take in total, at least model_timeout and at most 30m.

options.ai.classifier_model.description: A local linear classifier model (JSON) for evidence triage.

options.ai.classifier_endpoint.description: A provider-neutral classifier service URL for evidence triage.

options.ai.classifier_review.description: Routes evidence-first classifier triage to review; it never inserts relations itself.

options.ai.depth.description: The longest graph path a question searches.

options.ai.max_matches.description: The most graph path matches a question returns.

options.ai.max_paths_per_asset.description: The most witnessed paths kept for one asset.

options.ai.max_expansions.description: The most guided path expansions, bounded by the global policy.

options.ai.guidance_rounds.description: How many intermediate model navigation rounds a question may use; 0 turns guidance off.

options.ai.max_tokens.description: The most tokens in one model reply.

options.ai.temperature.description: The model's sampling temperature; 0 is the most reproducible.

options.ai.context_tokens.description: The Ollama context window in tokens. Every Ollama caller defaults to the same size, because Ollama reloads a model whenever a request asks for a different one.

options.ai.think.description: Lets an Ollama reasoning model think before answering (slower).

options.ai.attribution.description: Automatic decisions during enumerations: ownership, merges of duplicate organizations, admissions into scope and whether a name is a person's or an organization's. auto applies the strong ones and journals the rest for review, journal only journals them, off turns them off. It needs no model; with a main model, auto also lets the model decide admissions and names, and journal keeps its answers on names as advice.

options.ai.attribution_canary_every.description: Checks the cache that automatic decisions read through during an enumeration: every N passes, each organization's ownership gaps are also searched without the cache, and the engine log says whether the two searches matched. Each check costs a full search, so leave it off unless you are diagnosing missed or unexpected decisions. AMASS_ATTRIBUTION_CANARY_EVERY overrides it.

options.ai.journal.description: The review journal that proposals, AI decisions and document readings are recorded in.

options.ai.announce_decisions.description: Announces the classifier's applied decisions and new proposals (the end-of-run summary and assistant notices). AMASS_AI_ANNOUNCE_DECISIONS overrides it.

options.ai.classifier_applies.description: Lets a classifier trained from your review decisions (amass ai train) apply its confident answers on its own under attribution auto, for the questions where it otherwise only advises: whether a name is a person's or an organization's. Off, its answers are kept as advice and the main model, if set, decides. AMASS_AI_CLASSIFIER_APPLIES overrides it.

options.ai.contributions.strong_evidence.description: Lets what assistants add with the MCP contribute tool (recorded under amass-ai:<client> sources) be strong evidence. Off, a strong signal that only a contribution witnesses counts as supporting evidence: it still adds weight and corroborates other signals, but cannot on its own propose or apply an ownership relationship, widen scope or merge organizations. Contributed assets are investigated either way.

options.ai.documents.enabled.description: Turns on the one model allowed to read collected documents, all of each one's text, to find what they state in Open Asset Model terms: the assets they name, the relations between them and their field values. The documents are fetched again to be read (the database keeps no copy), and each version is read once. The main ai model never reads documents; without this section no model does.

options.ai.documents.provider.description: The document model's provider: ollama (the containerized Ollama or one on the host), compatible (an OpenAI-compatible chat API) or anthropic.

options.ai.documents.endpoint.description: The document model's endpoint. The Compose Ollama is http://ollama:11434; an Ollama on the host machine is http://host.docker.internal:11434 from a container or http://127.0.0.1:11434 outside one.

options.ai.documents.model.description: The document model's name at the provider. Required when the document model is enabled.

options.ai.documents.api_key_env.description: The environment variable holding the provider's API key, for a hosted provider. The key itself never goes in the config.

options.ai.documents.allow_http.description: Allows a plain HTTP endpoint, for a model on a trusted private network only (such as the Compose network).

options.ai.documents.model_timeout.description: How long one document model request, one chunk of a document, may take.

options.ai.documents.max_leads.description: During an enumeration the MCP server supervises, the document model hands the run each asset its findings name that the database does not hold and the engine collects from (domains, IP addresses, netblocks, ASNs, organizations, street addresses, phones, emails, URLs), as a lead the engine checks like any other. The number of leads adapts: it starts at 50, each lead the engine confirms earns 2 more while at least half of the leads checked are confirmed (below that, new leads wait), and it never passes one lead per 10 work items the run has completed. A positive value caps it lower; -1 submits no leads (findings are still stored). Each lead is tagged amass-ai, settled when the run ends, and can be retracted.

options.ai.documents.vision.description: Whether the document model can read pictures, for scanned PDFs whose pages are pictures of text. A model that can is shown each page and writes out its text; otherwise Tesseract reads the pages when it is installed (it is in the Compose images), and without either a scanned document gives no text. auto asks an Ollama model's capabilities, takes an Anthropic model as able and an OpenAI-compatible one as not.

options.ai.documents.context_tokens.description: The document model's context window, for an Ollama model: room for one chunk of a document, the instructions and the reply.

options.ai.documents.chunk_chars.description: How many characters of a document one request reads. A document is always read whole, chunk by chunk; a larger chunk means fewer requests but needs a larger context window.

options.ai.documents.max_tokens.description: The most tokens one document model reply may use. A reply cut off at the cap is incomplete, so that chunk is skipped and the rest of the document is still read; the cap stops a model that repeats itself from filling its whole context window.

options.ai.documents.share_with_assistan.description: Lets other models (the main investigation model and MCP clients) read the document model's findings, which quote the documents. Off, they see only counts.

options.ai.documents.hold.description: How long an enumeration the MCP server supervises stays open after collection is done while the document model still has documents to read, so the leads they give reach the run. It ends sooner once the documents left, at the pace they have been read, would not be read in time; the next run or read_documents reads them. 0 ends the run as soon as collection is done.

options.ai.documents.document_timeout.description: The longest one reading spends on one document. Past it no further part is started, and the document's next reading (a later pass of the same enumeration, or a later enumeration) continues where this one stopped, so nothing is skipped. A fast model reads whole documents within it; a slow one leaves the rest of a long document for later. 0 sets no limit.

options.ai.documents.max_chunks.description: The most parts (chunk_chars each) one reading takes from one document; the next reading continues where it stopped. Mainly bounds the tokens a hosted model is paid for. 0 sets no cap.
